what: Series of nightly mean paired differences, with the interval each should produce. What is authored is the series; the arithmetic applied to it is the shipped one.
whatItCannotSay: Nothing about what the lab's own difference series looks like. These say what the interval computes over a series, not what any series is. Until 2026-08-30 they also could not say anything about a series whose nights differ in pair count: every scenario carried one scalar `pairsPerNight`, which is the single population in which the sum of the pair counts and the harmonic mean the reported estimator carries are the same number, so the tier built to verify the effective count could not see the defect 3.14 corrected. `pairsByNight` is what closes that, and the two scenarios using it reuse an even scenario's series verbatim so the pair counts are the only thing that differs.
whyItIsOwed: Over the captured fixture every band 1 panel is withheld, because one night with no closed horizon cannot produce a series at all. So the block bootstrap and the effective-sample measurement, which are the decision this phase turns on, would be exercised by nothing. The failure that matters here is an interval that is too narrow, and a stage that never computes one cannot be too narrow or too wide.
theSeriesAreGeneratedFromAStatedRecipe: Each series is written out in full so the file is the input rather than a pointer to one, but each was produced by a stated recipe: a mean, a wobble either side of it, an optional AR(1) carry-over, and a fixed seed. The recipe is in the note so a reader can see what shape was intended, and the numbers are what the arithmetic actually ran on. `a-series-that-repeats-itself` needs the carry-over specifically: an independent series has no autocorrelation to measure, so the effective sample comes back equal to the night count and the measurement looks correct while asserting nothing. The two multi-pair series added for the effective-sample rewrite carry a pair count and a within-night dispersion as well, because a night that cannot say how its own pairs dispersed counts as one observation however many it has, and a file holding only the means could only ever exercise that corner.

scenarios.name: clearly-above-zero
scenarios.why: A series wobbling tightly around a positive mean. The lower bound should clear zero, which is what band 1 reads green on.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.02, wobble +/-0.004, independent nights, seed 1, 40 nights

scenarios.name: straddling-zero
scenarios.why: A series whose mean is barely positive against a wobble ten times its size. The interval should straddle zero and the panel should read that it does not clear it yet. This is the case a too-narrow interval gets wrong, and getting it wrong is how band 1 says the pattern is real before it is.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.001, wobble +/-0.02, independent nights, seed 2, 40 nights

scenarios.name: a-series-that-repeats-itself
scenarios.why: A series where each night carries most of the night before it. The effective sample should fall well below the night count, because nights that repeat each other carry one observation between them however many there are. Without a case of this shape the effective-sample measurement always returns the night count and looks correct.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.01, wobble +/-0.02, AR(1) with rho 0.85 so each night carries most of the one before, seed 3, 40 nights

scenarios.name: too-short-to-say-anything
scenarios.why: Fewer nights than twice the block length, so no interval is produced at all. Withheld rather than printed wide: a panel showing an interval built from a handful of nights invites a reading, and the count beside it is not enough to stop that.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.02, wobble +/-0.005, independent nights, seed 4, 12 nights

scenarios.name: many-names-a-night-moving-apart
scenarios.why: Eighty pairs a night whose nightly means vary by exactly what within-night independence predicts. The pairing has removed the market factor, so the night is worth its own pairs and the effective sample should be close to the row count rather than to the night count. Without a case of this shape the row count is never credited and the measurement collapses to the pessimistic corner on every series.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.004, uniform wobble +/-0.0193649 being exactly within/sqrt(pairs) rescaled for a uniform, 80 pairs a night at a within-night dispersion of 0.1, seed 5, 40 nights

scenarios.name: many-names-a-night-moving-together
scenarios.why: The same eighty pairs a night, but the nightly means vary three times wider than independence allows. The excess is common movement the matching failed to remove, so the row count is divided by about nine and the series falls back toward one observation a night. This is the case that stops the row count being a free credit: a night whose pairs all say the same thing is worth one of them.
scenarios.recipe: mean 0.004, uniform wobble +/-0.0580948 being three times what independence allows, 80 pairs a night at a within-night dispersion of 0.1, seed 6, 40 nights

scenarios.name: nights-that-differ-in-pair-count
scenarios.why: The same series as `many-names-a-night-moving-apart`, counted unevenly. Only the pair counts differ, so the mean and the bounds are identical and the effective count is the one quantity under test. Forty nights alternating eighty and five pairs is the case the 3.14 record names: the sum of the pair counts and the harmonic mean the reported estimator carries are furthest apart here, and before that repair the two were never compared.
scenarios.recipe: the nightlyMeans and withinNightDispersion of `many-names-a-night-moving-apart` verbatim, with pairsByNight alternating 80 and 5

scenarios.name: a-few-nights-too-thin-to-say
scenarios.why: The same series again, with five nights carrying a single pair among nights of eighty. A one-pair night says nothing about how its own pairs dispersed, so the design effect skips it, while the harmonic mean counts it and is dragged down hard by it. That interaction is what a uniform series cannot reach: the two discounts read the same series through different populations of nights.
scenarios.recipe: the nightlyMeans and withinNightDispersion of `many-names-a-night-moving-apart` verbatim, with pairsByNight of 1 on nights 4, 12, 20, 28 and 36 and 80 elsewhere
